lessons.title: Read a CTR before you build a dashboard
lessons.why: The CTR is the finished contact. Real-time metrics are a picture of now. They answer different questions.
paras: Fields you should be able to point at: ContactId, Channel, InitiationMethod, the endpoints, queue duration, the agent timestamps, ACW, disconnect reason, attributes, and the recording location. Transfers create another contact. PreviousContactId and NextContactId are the chain.
Delivery to Firehose or a stream is near real time and can duplicate. Consumers must be idempotent. Five minutes of silence is when you check the error prefix.
points: DisconnectReason is the first field when someone says the carrier dropped the call.
Attributes are whatever you wrote. They are not infinite.
A missing Recording.Location means recording was off or the write failed.
Do not average a day from real-time screenshots.
lessons.mistake: Building a warehouse table that keeps only the last contact in a transfer chain.

lessons.title: Real-time boards and historical intervals
lessons.why: Service level is a historical interval unless you say you are looking at the live queue.
paras: Historical metrics come in intervals such as 15 minutes. Real-time metrics show agents, queues, and profiles now. GetMetricDataV2 is the API for new work. Saved reports count toward the 2,000 report quota, including a supervisor's personal copies.
Queue duration is the usual wait clock. Handle time definitions vary. Write the formula next to the number.
points: Abandonment before the queue and abandonment in queue are different.
ACW is in occupancy. A dashboard that ignores it flatters the team.
Custom metrics exist and have a quota of 1,000.
The analytics data lake, previewed 28 November 2023, is the zero-ETL path into Athena or QuickSight.
lessons.mistake: Screenshotting the real-time page as the month's service level.

lessons.title: Conversational analytics is Contact Lens under a new name
lessons.why: The function did not vanish on 4 August 2026. The admin guide changed the name.
paras: Contact Lens was previewed 3 December 2019 and generally available 23 July 2020. Real-time rules arrived 1 December 2020. Chat analytics arrived 29 November 2022. Post-contact summaries became generally available 25 March 2024. The 4 August 2026 document-history note says Contact Lens is now conversational analytics.

You enable it per contact with the recording and analytics block. Real-time concurrent calls default to a quota of 300. Post-call jobs are sized from duration and volume. The planning formula in the quota page is duration times 0.4 times calls per hour, divided by 60.
points: Redaction is a setting. Confirm it before you promise it.
Categories are rules. They are not Lex intents.
Summaries can be wrong. The recording is the evidence.
A contact with analytics off produces no transcript to search.
lessons.mistake: Comparing a 2024 'Contact Lens' runbook to the console and concluding the feature was removed.

lessons.title: Agent events are the live staffing truth
lessons.why: The real-time board is a view. The event stream is the feed other systems can trust.
paras: Events include login, logout, status change, and connecting to a contact. WFM products such as Aspect and Eleveo consume this stream for adherence. You enable data streaming and point it at a Kinesis stream. Size the shards for the number of consumers.
ACW duration is derivable from the events. If your occupancy formula needs ACW, this is the source, not a guess from the wall board.
points: A missed logout event leaves someone 'available' in the third-party tool.
Status names must match the WFM map.
Do not let a test tool consume the production stream without its own iterator.
Firehose to S3 is the historical copy. The stream is the live copy.
lessons.mistake: Exporting a CSV once a night and calling it real-time adherence.
